research_question: Can two upstream-independent E011 STATIC_READY trefoil centrelines, treated as canonical-circulation regularized vortex filaments, generate an orientation-robust inverse-square attractive force from Kelvin impulse exchange without G?
objective: Test restricted two-filament interaction using real PKLSA static geometry, with a non-gravitational Euler-impulse quantity and separate Poisson underresolution diagnostics. No direct SST gravitation identification.
null_hypothesis: The specified Rosenhead-Kelvin candidate fails |n-2|<=0.2 or universal signed attraction under pi reorientation.
alternative_hypothesis: Both Gilbert and KnotPlot providers satisfy exponent 2 +/- 0.2 and same-sign attraction for all preregistered 0 and pi tilts, with <5% provider amplitude divergence at R/L=5.
assumptions: Prescribed fixed static knots are not certified Euler equilibria
Rosenhead epsilon=canonical core radius is a chosen regularization, not unique finite core profile
Geometric reach is identified with physical hydrodynamic core radius only as an explicit scenario
No gravity G enters candidate solver
Kelvin impulse exchange is not by itself the force on a material particle or a proof of gravitation
E011 static geometry is not DYNAMICS_READY
Periodic Poisson grid is diagnostic and underresolved

equations.latex: \mathbf v_A(\mathbf x)=\frac{\Gamma_A}{4\pi}\oint_A\frac{d\mathbf X_A\times(\mathbf x-\mathbf X_A)}{(|\mathbf x-\mathbf X_A|^2+r_c^2)^{3/2}}

observables.definition: Interaction-only Kelvin impulse derivative parallel to separation
Far-field exponent of the longitudinal exchange observable

steps.operation: Validate two raw E011 SHA-256 against frozen provider_pins; parse Fourier/GVECT and resample
Evaluate regularized Biot-Savart at target segment midpoints
Evaluate Kelvin impulse cross derivative separately on each knot and action-reaction residual
Sweep distance and orientation, estimate log slope and conditional gradient
Run grid Poisson cross-pressure exploratory FFT inversion with explicit underresolution flag
Compile independent C++ source, test quantitative parity
Compare separate independent provider families; one vote per provider

falsification_criteria.criterion: For both upstream providers, abs(n-2)>0.2 for n fitted R/L>=8 with sign-stable nonzero forces
The axial exchange force changes sign between 0 and pi tilt at fixed Gamma signs and R/L=5
Relative provider force amplitude difference at R/L=5 exceeds 0.05

edge_cases: Knot chirality / signed writhe are different across raw provider anchors
Canonical core unresolved on <1 gridcell exploratory Poisson
Large-distance cancellation, use analytical leading multipole check
Orientation of filament and sign of circulation are physically distinct
No identification of single vortex-knot mass with gram-sized experiment
predictions: Dipolar filament-induced velocity decays as R^-3 and generic mutual impulse transfer as R^-4
Attraction is not universal and orientation can reverse sign
Without independent mass closure G cannot be inferred from filament force amplitudes
